correctness.rationale: Edmonds' exact rank-inequality description is used in the correct intrinsic affine hull. Each subset normal is orthogonally projected to the zero-sum translation space, giving norm \(c(S)=\sqrt{|S|(n-|S|)/n}\). A radius-\(t\) ball is therefore feasible exactly when all shifted rank inequalities hold. The resulting finite linear program is dualized explicitly: free center coordinates impose equal element-cover weights, normalization gives fractional partitions, and strong duality yields the ratio. The complete center set follows by fixing the optimal radius in the same exact inequalities. Connectedness guarantees full intrinsic dimension and positive inradius; finite examples are not used as proof.

value.rationale: The theorem converts a canonical Euclidean invariant of every connected matroid base polytope into a purely rank-theoretic fractional-partition optimization and simultaneously describes all Chebyshev centers. It applies in arbitrary rank, contains hypersimplices as an exact closed-form specialization, and exposes a geometric weighting of rank deficits distinct from classical strength objectives. This is a structural all-rank result rather than a finite table, parameter substitution, or isolated computation.
